answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable bond before it may vote on a task, with one bond-backed vote per task and penalties for proven collusion. The bond does not prove a person is unique, but makes mass identities costly: an attacker must lock up capital for every Sybil and risks losing it if those identities coordinate deceptively. At a summit, a lagoon or an opal market, the same rule applies; the attacker pays in tied-up funds and possible forfeiture.
